what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission heard a forester's presentation on a proposed Rob's Hill timber harvest and largely opposed public comment; no vote was taken.
The chair said nothing was being voted on, and the harvest plan is to be reviewed again at a later meeting after comments.
Residents asked about expected revenue; the forester said values come only after a cutting plan and bids, and that first-cut money is earmarked for bridge, gate and accessibility work.
The commission continued the 141 Hemlock Dr notice of intent, the Hickory Hills drawdown plan and the 200 Townsend Road request to October 3rd.
The commission approved a septic upgrade at 217 Reservoir Road, lifted an enforcement order at 255 Sunset Lane, and issued a new enforcement order on a Pleasant Street owner.

why_it_matters: A harvest on town conservation land, and the timber revenue it might bring toward town-forest projects, has not been decided, so residents can still comment before any plan is approved.
Revenue was described as funding forest management, while the commission said income was not the driver, so the money figures are still unknown until a cutting plan and bids exist.
watch_next: October 3rd, when the continued wetland hearings return to the commission.
A later meeting at which the Rob's Hill harvest plan is reviewed again after the comments.
